To our knowl- edge, there is no query-bag matching study exists, and we focus on the new approach in this paper. hCNN is a CNN based matching model which is fast enough to work on the industry application. The input of hCNN is a query q and the i-th question bi in the bag. q and bi are fed into a CNN respectively. A cross-attention matrix Mi is fed into another CNN to get the interaction representation between them. Each element of Mi is defined as Mi a,b = q⊤a · bi,b where qa is the word embedding of the a-th word in query q and bi,b is the embedding of the b-th word in bi.

The rr is then concatenated to the matching representation rp as a new feature to predict the query-bag matching degree.

retrieval_query: Does the query-bag matching model use a neural network?
answer: Yes, the query-bag matching model uses a neural network. Its core component hCNN is a CNN-based matching model: the query q and the i-th question b_i in the bag are fed into a CNN respectively, and a cross-attention matrix M_i is fed into another CNN to obtain the interaction representation [4]. In addition, an hCNN is used to model the relationship between the user query and the new "question" b_r (built via TF-IDF) to obtain the matching representation r_r used to predict the query-bag matching degree [5].
